Writing v = dx/dt is correct. The missing piece is that t represents a physical time, so t² carries units of s².

For x(t) = (1 m/s³)t³,

v(t) = (1 m/s³) × 3t².

The 3 is dimensionless; t² has units s². Thus the velocity units are (m/s³)(s²) = m/s. Writing only “3t²” hides the coefficient and its units. At t = 2 s, for example, v = 3(1 m/s³)(2 s)² = 12 m/s.
